rv.q: With City Lit’s production drawing clear parallels to today’s headlines, especially through projections designed by Andres Fiz, this 25-year-old play feels disturbingly relevant.
Stephen Adly Guirgis’ “Jesus Hopped the ‘A’ Train,” beautifully mounted by City Lit, shows us what live theater can be.

Cruz's sure-handed and imaginative production gives all the actors in the ensemble a chance to shine, and it's a particular triumph for Izquierdo and Stevens, who make every moment of their jailhouse encounters count.
This is one of the most thought-provoking productions of the year thus far.
It is an amazing production, and you should see it now!

cn.t: Critics praise this dynamic revival of Guirgis's powerful drama, citing excellent performances and inventive staging that bring the harrowing Rikers Island story to life with emotional depth and challenging questions about justice and redemption.
